name: Statement run (page-per-master dossier)
description: One page (or page group) per master entity: master name as the page title, master-level facts under it, then each child entity's own section with a lines table. The workhorse for customer statements, per-supplier dossiers, per-employee packets.
whenToUse: The ask contains 'one page per X', 'X name as page header/title', or child entities grouped under a master. Decide BEFORE the data model: this archetype demands NESTED output groups — flat data cannot feed it.
intents: one page per customer with their invoices and lines
each supplier on its own page with details grouped under it
customer name as page title, invoices listed below with line items
statement per account with transactions grouped by document

requires.dataShape: nested datamodel output groups MASTER > CHILD > LINE via layered groupBy (e.g. G_CUSTOMER > G_INVOICE > G_LINE); ORDER BY the group columns in SQL
requires.preAggregation: master-level totals as SQL columns on the master group where possible (SUM OVER / ROLLUP), not template math

composition.notes: combine with a page header/footer technique for page furniture; chart-on-first-page composes as a TOP-LEVEL chart block before the outer forEach

pitfalls: Inner forEach/table groups are RELATIVE (no leading /) — an absolute inner group is rejected by the builder.
Never fake depth from flat data with ../FIELD + preceding-sibling guards — renders a collapsed table (verified failure). Restructure the data model instead.
Bind placeholder names (G_MASTER, MASTER_NAME) to YOUR datamodel's actual output tree before building.

sourceRefs.verifiedIn: live E2E 2026-08-05: 119-page pod render, pie page 1 + per-customer sections

name: Multi-level nested sections (blocks[] forEach nesting)
description: Three-plus level master-detail inside one RTF: nested forEach blocks mirror the datamodel's nested groups; each level adds headings/facts; the innermost level is a lines table.
whenToUse: Any hierarchy deeper than the simple invoice shape (one master + one lines level). The data model MUST provide the same nesting via groupBy.
intents: customer then invoices then invoice lines nested sections
three level grouping in one document
master detail detail report structure
sections inside sections with their own tables

requires.dataShape: nested output groups matching every forEach level

composition.notes: splitByPage:true on the OUTER forEach = page break per master; on a table block it means one page per ROW — different semantics

pitfalls: heading/paragraph text is runs[] — literals and {field,format?} objects; there is NO {FIELD} string interpolation.
The page-break knob is splitByPage — there is no pageBreakAfter.

sourceRefs.verifiedIn: user web test rerun 2026-08-04: 417-page render, 12 customers on fresh pages

name: Table totals row (sum/count with label span and shading)
description: A bold totals row under a lines table: label cell (optionally spanning several leading columns) plus aggregate cells; optional background shade.
whenToUse: Any lines table where the user asks for totals/subtotals per section. Prefer SQL/rollup columns for GRAND totals across sections.
intents: totals row under the invoice lines table
sum the amount column at the bottom
subtotal per section with shaded totals line
pitfalls: span merges LEADING label cells — count your columns.
A total that must cross sections (grand total) belongs in SQL (ROLLUP/SUM OVER), not in the template.

name: RTF chart block (pie/bar/line, grouped or raw)
description: A real vector chart inside an RTF template: shape-alt-text Graph encoding rendered by the BIP engine. Grouped mode aggregates a measure per category; raw mode plots one bar per row.
whenToUse: 'Add a chart/pie/graph' to a print report or its first page. TOP-LEVEL placement only.
intents: pie chart of amount by customer on the first page
bar chart of totals per department in the pdf
add a graph above the table in the report

composition.notes: place BEFORE any forEach; chart inside a forEach re-emits per iteration (verified duplication)

pitfalls: Keys are graphType / group:{select,by} / measures:[{label,field,agg:sum|count|avg}] — NOT the XPT vocabulary (type/dimensionField/string group); the builder rejects wrong keys with a teaching error.
A select matching 0 nodes renders a normal-looking frame with literal 'No data to display' at HTTP 200 — verify group.select against the data XML and LOOK at the chart area after render.
summarizeReportLayout/extractText cannot see charts (alt-text shape, no <?tags?>) — tagCount 0 is normal.

sourceRefs.verifiedIn: chartproof matrix + live pod E2E 2026-08-04 (pie page 1, real data)

name: XPT side-by-side: chart + repeating detail table (LayoutGrid)
description: The classic monitoring-dashboard row: an interactive chart in the left cell and a REPEATING detail table in the right cell of one LayoutGrid row. Exports to a clean PDF too.
whenToUse: 'Dashboard: chart on the left, details on the right'. This shape is XPT-ONLY — an RTF grid cell cannot host a repeating table (BIP collapses it).
intents: dashboard with chart left and detail table right
chart beside a repeating data table on one page
monitoring dashboard side by side layout

requires.dataShape: one detail-grain group feeds both: the chart aggregates it, the table lists it; charts want long/detail rows, not pre-aggregated wide columns

conflicts: rtf grid with repeating table in a cell
composition.notes: grid columns are PIXELS (sum ~1554 for a 1650px page); each chart binds EXACTLY 1 measure (multi-series via seriesField); DataTable filtering via filters[] — an XPath predicate yields 0 rows

pitfalls: Column widths in PIXELS here — twips values (4200/7800) push cells off-page and render blank.
2+ measures on one XPT chart faults when a sibling chart shares the page — builder rejects it; use seriesField.
No local render for .xpt — verify on the pod (prepareReportForPod -> runReport).

sourceRefs.verifiedIn: ESS dashboard matrix sessions; corpus exemplars (Oracle ESS dashboard)

name: Wide pivot computed in the template (per-cell XSLT sums)
description: Building a many-column pivot (column per SKU/month/period) as per-cell cross-group XSLT sums inside the template.
intents: pivot by SKU columns in the layout
one column per month computed in the template
matrix report built with template formulas per cell
trigger: a pivot/matrix ask ('column per X') heading toward template-side computation
why: It renders, but tens of near-identical XSLT sum() cells are unmaintainable by a human (verified: the Tama Cotton File pivot) and silently break on Word edits — banned by the simplicity contract.
alternative: Pivot in SQL — native PIVOT or SUM(CASE WHEN key='…' THEN qty END) columns; the template then shows a flat table. For interactive use, XPT's native Crosstab is legitimate.

name: Faking hierarchy with ../FIELD + preceding-sibling guards
description: Emulating a 3-level document over FLAT data by reaching up with ../PARENT_FIELD and suppressing repeats with position()/preceding-sibling tricks.
intents: show parent fields inside a flat detail loop
suppress repeating header values with preceding-sibling
three level report from a flat dataset
trigger: a multi-level ask being forced into the flat invoice shape (outerGroup/linesGroup) instead of nested groups
why: Collapses into a broken table — misaligned headers, repeated/blank cells (verified failure, user web test 2026-08-04). The builder now rejects the absolute-inner-group variant.
alternative: Model the hierarchy in the DATA: layered datamodel groupBy (G_A > G_B > G_C), then nested forEach blocks.

name: Carry-forward / brought-forward page totals
description: Running page totals printed at the bottom of each page ('carried forward') and repeated at the top of the next ('brought forward') — a standard BIP capability via <?add-page-total?>/<?show-page-total?> that our generator does not emit yet.
whenToUse: Financial listings that must show running totals per printed page. BIP supports it; our DSL has no block for it yet — say so honestly and offer the nearest alternative (per-section totals via the totals row, or a running SQL SUM OVER column).
intents: carried forward brought forward totals on each page
running total at the bottom of every printed page
page totals that continue to the next page
pitfalls: Do NOT attempt to fake page totals with template math — page boundaries are a rendering concept invisible to XSLT.
